text: An in-house lab started in the visit lands on the chart and on the bill together. Nothing is filled in for you, so what's charted is what you actually saw.
Maple Rivera is drinking a lot. Dr. Lane wants a blood glucose and a heartworm test.
Remember: type what you measured. Number rows start blank.
In Checkout, add the lab as a charge.
Pick Blood glucose.
The line says Not run: ordered, but not done yet.
Click the arrow to open the form.
The value is blank. It never starts at zero.
Type the reading.
And Save results.
It says Complete, and it's on Maple's chart. Scout doesn't judge numbers. Dr. Lane does.
Now the heartworm test. Add it the same way.
Pick Heartworm 4Dx.
Open its form.
Fill normal values sets every choice row to its normal answer, here Negative.
Maple's heartworm is positive, so change that row.
An abnormal answer is flagged, so the doctor sees it.
Save results.
The chip says 1 abnormal. Choice answers like Positive are judged, and a normal 4Dx would say Normal.
On a form with numbers, like the urine dipstick, Fill normal values leaves the numbers blank. Type each one.
The most common mistake: clicking Fill normal values and saving without typing the numbers. Remember: type what you measured. Number rows start blank.
